comments.text:
How come people can still deny the obvious, even though it has worked like this for a long time? I hear a lot of denial when it comes to people losing their jobs, but at least for a while this will be the case. You can't deny the last 200 years of corporate 'tradition', so investing in AI to be implemented in your company means that company is going to want to spend less money elsewhere. Looking at the amounts of money that is thrown at AI and Robotics, it may well turn into the biggest lay-off fever ever, and though it may start with software engineers, they will merely be the first of a long list of jobs that will disappear because of AI.

That's the problem with everything in capitalism (no, I am not a communist), that it's not about providing society with its material needs, or about people or jobs, but about making profit. The general focus has been wrong ever since capitalism was introduced, but within a globalized economy it has become more evident than ever because local governments are no longer able to (more or less) correct the wrongs (Keynes, f.e.) that the globalized capitalist economy (promoted by, and worsened through neoliberalism) has within its core structures, goals, and paradigms.

Self-enrichment is by definition the wrong focus and incentive for a healthy (and sustainable) economy and society. The economy is also an educator within the culture, and it educates towards increased selfishness, and nepotism, and much more things that stand in the way of a free and just society. This particular economy is an eco-system that favors and promotes some of the most destructive and dangerous characteristics people can have, and the leaders of that economy and society will in most case be some of the worst humanity has to offer. In short, we desperately need a new kind of economy with a primary focus on providing society with its material needs, instead of 'producing and selling stuff' (much of which we don't actually need) for profit.
